small_guidance:
- The current fused bias-tanh epilogue is fine; the bottleneck is the ConvTranspose2d itself. Minor tuning (BLOCK=8192, num_warps=4) on the epilogue will not move fast_p much since conv dominates runtime.
- Consider folding the bias subtraction into a pre-baked conv bias: set `conv_transpose.bias = conv_transpose.bias - self.bias.view(-1)` once (at eval) so only tanh remains in the epilogue kernel — saves a load per element.
- Ensure the conv input/weight are in channels_last memory format and cast to TF32-friendly path; pre-set `conv_transpose` to `.to(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` to let cuDNN pick faster algos.
large_guidance:
- Replace the `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton kernel implemented as a scatter-add of `input × kernel` outer products into the output grid, handling stride=2/padding=1/output_padding=1 in index math. The conv dominates the 23.5 ms runtime; fusing bias-sub and tanh into the scatter epilogue eliminates the entire post-pass.
- Alternative: implement transposed conv as a gather-style GEMM where each output pixel `(n, oc, oh, ow)` sums over `(ic, kh, kw)` of `input[n, ic, (oh+pad-kh)/stride, (ow+pad-kw)/stride] * weight[ic, oc, kh, kw]` with divisibility masks. One program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile); autotune BLOCK_M/N/K = {64,128}×{64,128}×{16,32}, num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}. Fuse bias subtract + tanh in the epilogue on the accumulator before store.
- Use channels_last layout for both the input and output so the IC and OC axes are contiguous along GEMM-K and GEMM-N, enabling coalesced loads of the input and vectorized stores of the fused output.
